study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
cohort: 1,996 women who delivered term singleton infants at the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics between May 1, 2020, and April 30, 2021
finding: Increased maternal BMI at delivery was significantly associated with several adverse perinatal outcomes, including nonreassuring fetal status, cesarean birth, postpartum hemorrhage, hypertensive diseases of pregnancy, and neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal BMI at delivery was significantly associated with both unscheduled and overall cesarean birth rates.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight increased with increasing maternal BMI.
